arguments.text:
Fixed. In `src/plugin/timezone/index.js`, `dayjs.tz(input, timezone)` treated every input as a wall-clock string: it ran `d.utc(input)` on the input, so a numeric timestamp / JS `Date` / Day.js object (already an absolute instant) was re-interpreted as a naive local time and shifted by the target zone's offset (e.g. `dayjs.tz(1401638400000, 'America/New_York')` gave `2014-06-01T16:00:00-04:00` instead of `2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00`).

Fix: non-string inputs are now treated as absolute instants and converted with `d(input).tz(timezone)`; only strings go through the `fixOffset` wall-clock path.

Verified: the `Parse parse timestamp, js Date, Day.js object` behaviour now holds for timestamp, `Date` and Day.js object inputs (all give `2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00`, `1401638400000`, offset `-240`), and the full pre-existing suite is green — 56 suites / 524 tests pass, including `test/plugin/timezone.test.js` under TZ=Pacific/Auckland, Europe/London, America/Whitehorse and the default TZ. Lint on the changed file is clean.
`weekStart: 1` — the Burmese locale starts the week on Monday (index 1).

#4 still in progress. I've reproduced it: `dayjs(...).tz(zone)` reports the wrong UTC offset in the formatted string (`format('Z')`/`format()`) whenever the host TZ's current offset differs from the offset at the target instant — e.g. under TZ=Pacific/Auckland, `dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz('America/Los_Angeles')` gives `2014-06-01T05:00:00-06:00` instead of `-07:00`. Root cause is in the plugin's `proto.tz`, which derives the offset via `new Date(target).valueOf()` (local-time parsing of a `toLocaleString` result). Working on the fix now; ETA ~10 min.

arguments.text: #4 still in progress. Reproduced and root-caused: `proto.tz` in the timezone plugin computes the target offset via `new Date(target).valueOf()`, where `target` comes from `toLocaleString('en-US', ...)`; that local-time parse is wrong whenever the host TZ offset at that instant differs from the offset at "now" (e.g. TZ=Pacific/Auckland: `dayjs('2014-06-01T12:00:00Z').tz('America/Los_Angeles')` → `-06:00` instead of `-07:00`). I'm rewriting it to use the plugin's `tzOffset` helper (Intl-based) and verifying against moment-timezone under several host TZs. ETA ~12 min.

#8 fixed and verified. `src/locale/nl.js` had `ordinal: n => \`${n}.\`` (a period), but Dutch ordinals are `1ste, 2de, 3de, 4de, ..., 8ste, ..., 20ste, 21ste, 22ste, ...`. Changed to `ordinal: n => \`[${n}${n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20 ? 'ste' : 'de'}]\`` (bracketed so the advancedFormat plugin's `Do`/`wo` output is not re-parsed as format tokens). Verified `dayjs(d).locale('nl').format('Do')` matches moment for days 1–31 and for "today", and `advancedFormat.test.js` still passes.

#11 fixed and verified. `src/plugin/weekYear/index.js` only handled the "week 1 of next year" case; it lacked the symmetric "last week of previous year" case, so dates in early January belonging to the previous ISO week-year returned the wrong year (e.g. with `yearStart: 4`, `2016-01-01` returned 2016 instead of 2015). Added: if the month is January and the week-of-year is >= 52, return `year - 1`. Verified `weekYear()` matches moment for every valid date 2015–2021 under locales `en`, `en-gb` (yearStart 4) and `zh-cn`, and `weekYear.test.js` / `weekOfYear.test.js` / `advancedFormat.test.js` still pass.
